dataset_summary.source_description: Ma et al. TWITTER15 propagation-tree dataset (tree structure & relative timestamps only; veracity labels and tweet text excluded).
dataset_summary.reconstruction_note: Uses explicit parent-child propagation links recorded in tree/<id>.txt (retweets/replies). Note: Twitter API hydration constraints mean user profile features are excluded and some deleted branches may be absent from the original collection; delays are recorded at minute precision.

actions_taken: Dropped 18188 duplicate edge(s), keeping earliest timestamp.
Resolved 4866 multi-parent conflict(s) by retaining the earliest-timestamp parent.
Detected 666 directed cycle(s) and removed 666 latest-timestamp cycle edge(s).
warnings: 13 cascade(s) contain multiple roots (disconnected components / forest).

baseline_comparison_note: WARNING: Random Forest did NOT beat the naive num_edges-only baseline on temporal test PR-AUC (0.828 vs 0.876). Structural topology added no measurable lift over early volume alone at T=1800s.

feature_importance.note: Clustering is always 0.0 on trees (flagged as uninformative rather than hidden).

limitations: Evidence comes strictly from the specific public dataset and time period loaded; results do not generalize automatically across platforms or eras.
Private-channel sharing (e.g., direct messages, WhatsApp/Telegram) is unobserved.
Structure-only models exclude tweet text, media, seed-account follower count, and external amplification, creating an inherent performance ceiling.
Predicted virality measures spreading behaviour, never truthfulness; fast-spreading true news also scores high.
Thresholds and probability calibration drift as platform UI and sharing behaviour evolve.
Dual-use risk: virality predictors can guide amplification of misleading content.
disclaimer: This system predicts propagation behaviour from early graph structure and timestamps only. It does not evaluate truthfulness and must not be used for fake-news or rumor verification.
